title: When the Portrait Sings
premise: Isandro Ashgrove, a meticulous property surveyor who trusts measurements over feelings, is sent to appraise Hollowmere House on the eve of its demolition. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside, the house begins counting him back — his footsteps, his heartbeats, his name — and he discovers he is the last verse of a song the house has been singing for two hundred years. As he bonds with the excavation crew's estranged descendants of the family that sealed the door, Isandro must choose between completing the song (which will make him part of the house forever) and learning its final verse without singing along. In the end, he sings the verse wrong on purpose — off-key, human, imperfect — and the house, having never heard anything sung out of love rather than duty, lets him go, collapsing into silence with the found family watching from the road.
about_author: Vesper Montrose is the pen name of a former building inspector who spent eleven years cataloguing condemned properties across the English moors before turning to horror. They write in empty houses on purpose, and claim to have never met one that sang back.

chapters.title: The House That Counts
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He arrives at Hollowmere House for a routine pre-demolition appraisal, noting its odd symmetry and the way doors seem to settle shut behind him. He counts rooms twice; the numbers disagree by one. Emotional beat: quiet unease masked by professional detachment — Isandro's ritualized counting established as armor against a chaotic childhood.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The excavation crew's backhoe strikes something beneath the foundation: a door, iron-banded, bolted from within. The crew chief, Mara Vane, refuses to touch it. That night Isandro dreams of humming he can't stop. Emotional beat: dread deepens as professional curiosity wars with instinct.

chapters.title: Appraisal of Souls
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara reveals her family has held the demolition contract for generations and always refused this parcel. She shows Isandro her grandmother's ledger: every surveyor who appraised Hollowmere vanished mid-report. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forms between skeptic and believer.

chapters.title: The Song Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Alone at dusk, Isandro hears a lullaby rising through the joists — wordless except for one recurring phrase. He records it on his phone; playback shows forty seconds of static shaped like breath. Emotional beat: isolation curdling into compulsion as the melody lodges in his head.

chapters.title: Doors Counted, Doors Owed
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The house begins returning his counts: he logs eleven doors, finds twelve. His own handwriting appears in his survey notes describing rooms he never entered. Emotional beat: the hunter becomes the measured — Isandro realizes the house is appraising him.

chapters.title: The Vane Inheritance
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara digs into the family archive: in 1823, her ancestor Elowen Vane sealed her singing daughter behind the door to stop a plague of grief that spread through song. The Vanes were paid to keep it buried — duty as inheritance. Emotional beat: Mara's resentment of her bloodline's burden surfaces.

chapters.title: Verse One
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro catches himself humming the phrase aloud and the house responds — lights warming, doors opening like held breath. A mirror shows him standing in a room he isn't in. Emotional beat: terror mixed with a shameful thrill of being wanted.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The excavation crew — Mara, her brother Teo, and old foreman Bram — camp on-site against protocol. Over cards and bad stew, they become a makeshift family around Isandro, who has never had one. Emotional beat: warmth as counterweight to horror; found family theme takes root.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Left Out
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara finds Elowen's diary: the daughter wasn't mad — she was loved so completely the house learned love from her and began demanding it. Sealing her didn't end the song; it froze it mid-verse. Emotional beat: moral vertigo — the ancestors' duty was also a betrayal.

chapters.title: The Room That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Following his own forged handwriting, Isandro finds the twelfth door inside the house — a twin of the excavated one, warm to the touch. Through it he hears a child singing the second verse. Emotional beat: compassion displaces fear; he wants to answer.

chapters.title: Teo Hums Back
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. Young Teo, lonely and reckless, hums the melody at the fire. The ground answers; frost blooms in July; Bram drags him away but Teo has already learned three lines. Emotional beat: guilt and protectiveness — Isandro's secret has endangered someone he loves.

chapters.title: Time Already Running Out
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro's reflection now lags half a second behind him, and his survey report writes itself each night, one line closer to completion. Bram deciphers the pattern: when the report ends, so does Isandro. Emotional beat: countdown pressure; the stakes turn personal and mortal.

chapters.title: Elowen's Mistake
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara translates the diary's final pages: Elowen tried to finish the song herself to free her daughter and was taken instead — the house keeps whoever completes it. The last verse exists nowhere; it must be invented. Emotional beat: despair pivoting into defiant hope.

chapters.title: Learning Without Singing Along
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro trains himself to listen without echoing — writing the verses down, mouthing silently, Mara holding his jaw shut during sleep-singing. Each verse learned costs him a memory: his mother's voice goes first. Emotional beat: sacrifice made visible; identity eroding.

chapters.title: Bram's Bargain
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Old Bram confesses he surveyed Hollowmere forty years ago and survived by promising the house a replacement someday. It has waited for Isandro ever since. Emotional beat: betrayal and forgiveness entwined; Bram offers himself back to void the debt.

chapters.title: The Demolition Order
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. City officials arrive to accelerate demolition after complaints of nighttime singing heard across town. The crew realizes blasting the door will release everything unfinished at once. Emotional beat: external deadline collides with internal one — no safe options left.

chapters.title: Verse Four, Unwritten
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the threshold of the inner room, Isandro finally sees her: the daughter, grown old in a single unaging moment, still waiting for someone to finish what her mother started. She teaches him the third verse freely, weeping. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into tenderness; the monster revealed as a child of abandonment.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Blast
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The crew spends their last ordinary night together — Teo teaching Isandro card tricks, Mara reading Elowen's diary aloud like a bedtime story, Bram keeping watch. Isandro nearly forgets he is dying. Emotional beat: fullness of found family; everything now worth losing.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At dawn, with the blast wired and the report one line from done, Isandro enters the twelfth room and begins the song. The house rises through him, hungry for completion. Emotional beat: climax — duty, love, and selfhood pulling in three directions at once.

chapters.title: Sung Wrong on Purpose
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the final line, Isandro sings it deliberately wrong — cracked, off-key, laughing through tears — because a song finished perfectly belongs to the house, but a song ruined lovingly belongs to the singer. The daughter laughs too, for the first time in two centuries. Emotional beat: triumph through imperfection; love against duty resolved.

chapters.title: Collapse Into Silence
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Hollowmere folds inward without violence, taking the door, the song, and Elowen's daughter home. Bram's debt burns to ash; Teo forgets the melody mid-hum. Isandro walks out of the dust missing memories but carrying the crew. Emotional beat: cathartic release; the house dies forgiven.

chapters.title: The Surveyor's Report
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Weeks later, Isandro files his final report on the empty lot — one honest page, no ghosts in the margins. Mara, Teo, and Bram help him move into a small house with exactly the right number of doors. Sometimes, very faintly, he hums something new. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — identity rebuilt not by forgetting, but by choosing who sings next.
